title.zh: 卷七十六 循吏列傳
title.raw: 卷七十六 循吏列傳 Volume 76: Biographies of Upright Officials

sentences.zh: 初，光武長于民間，頗達情僞，見稼穡艱難，百姓病害，至天下已定，務用安靜，解王莽之繁密，還漢世之輕法。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangwu had grown up among the common people and was fairly versed in true and false; he had seen the hardship of farming and the ills of the people. When the realm was finally settled, he strove for quiet rule, undid Wang Mang’s tangled severity, and restored the Han era’s lighter laws.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu had been raised among ordinary folk, so he grasped what was real and what was not, and he had watched tillers suffer and the people sicken. Once the empire was his, he pursued calm government: he loosened Wang Mang’s suffocating code and brought back the Han tradition of relatively mild punishments.

sentences.zh: 身衣大練，色無重綵，耳不聽鄭、衛之音，手不持珠玉之玩，宫房無私爱，左右無偏恩。

translations.literal: He personally wore thick plain silk; his garb held no doubled colors. His ears did not listen to the music of Zheng and Wei; his hands did not hold jade and pearl trinkets. The inner palace had no private favorites; those at his side received no lopsided grace.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed in single layers of homespun, shunned gaudy dyes, shut out the licentious airs of Zheng and Wei, and kept his hands from jeweled playthings. He showed no private infatuation in the harem and no uneven favor to attendants.

sentences.zh: 建武十三年，異國有獻名馬者，日行千里，又進寶劒，賈兼百金，詔以馬駕鼓車，劒賜騎士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth Jianwu year, a foreign land presented a famous horse that could travel a thousand in a day; it also offered a precious sword worth a hundredweight of gold. An edict used the horse to pull the drum cart and bestowed the sword on a horseman.
translations.idiomatic: In 37 a tributary state sent a thousand-li stallion and a blade worth a hundred catties of gold; the court hitched the horse to the ritual drum cart and gave the sword to a cavalryman instead of hoarding both.

sentences.zh: 損上林池籞之官，廢騁望弋獵之事。

translations.literal: He reduced the posts for Shanglin’s pools and preserves and abolished the business of coursing, gazing, and fowling for sport.
translations.idiomatic: He cut keepers of the imperial parks and put an end to pleasure hunts and hawking.

sentences.zh: 其以手迹賜方國者，皆一札十行，細書成文。

translations.literal: Those to whom he granted his own hand to vassal states all received a single tablet of ten lines, fine script forming the text.
translations.idiomatic: Letters to regional rulers were compact—one slip, ten lines, in his own tight hand.

sentences.zh: 勤約之風，行于上下。

translations.literal: Diligent frugality’s wind ran through high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Thrift and restraint ran from the throne to the clerks.

sentences.zh: 數引公卿郎將，列于禁坐。

translations.literal: He often summoned ministers, counselors, and generals, arraying them in the inner seat.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly called nobles, ministers, and generals to sit in the privy audience.

sentences.zh: 廣求民瘼，觀納風謠。

translations.literal: He broadly sought the people’s ailments and looked to take in the songs and laments of custom.
translations.idiomatic: He asked after popular hardship and listened to local ballads and complaints.

sentences.zh: 故能内外匪懈，百姓寬息。

translations.literal: Therefore inside and outside none slacked; the common people were relaxed and at rest.
translations.idiomatic: So court and countryside stayed alert in duty, while commoners could breathe again.

sentences.zh: 自臨宰邦邑者，競能其官。

translations.literal: As for those who personally governed districts and cities, vied in fulfilling their office.
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates, for their part, rivaled one another in competence.

sentences.zh: 若杜詩守南陽，號爲“杜母”，任延、錫光移變邊俗，斯其績用之最章章者也。

translations.literal: Such as Du Shi guarding Nanyang, called “Mother Du”; Ren Yan and Xi Guang remade frontier custom—these are the most shining examples of their achievement and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shi in Nanyang was nicknamed the “Nourishing Mother”; Ren Yan and Xi Guang transformed borderlands—their records stand out clearest among model officials.

sentences.zh: 又第五倫、宋均之徒，亦足有可稱談。

translations.literal: Also men like Di Lun and Song Jun are enough to merit mention in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The likes of Di Lun and Song Jun likewise deserve a word.

sentences.zh: 然建武、永平之間，吏事刻深，亟以謠言單辭，轉易守長。

translations.literal: Yet between Jianwu and Yongping, official business was severe and cutting; on slight rumor or single testimony, magistrates were often replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Still, in the Jianwu–Yongping years governance turned harsh: one whisper or isolated accusation could cost a magistrate his post.

sentences.zh: 故朱浮數上諫書，箴切峻政，鍾離意等亦規諷殷勤，以長者爲言，而不能得也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhu Fu several times presented remonstrance, needling the harsh government; Zhongli Yi and others also earnestly counseled in oblique remonstrance, pleading the example of the elder sort—yet they could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu repeatedly protested the severity; Zhongli Yi and others pressed the same in careful language—useless against the trend.

sentences.zh: 所以中興之美，蓋未盡焉。

translations.literal: So the beauty of the restoration is probably not complete.
translations.idiomatic: The “restored golden age” therefore remains imperfect.

sentences.zh: 自章、和以後，其有善績者，徃徃不絕。

translations.literal: From Zhang and He onward, those with good records have never ceased to appear.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhangde and Yonghe reigns, capable magistrates kept appearing.

sentences.zh: 如魯恭、吳祐、劉寬及潁川四長，並以仁信篤誠，使人不欺；

translations.literal: Such as Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan, and the “four elders” of Yingchuan—all by benevolence, trust, and earnest good faith made men cease to deceive one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gong, Wu You, Liu Kuan, and the Yingchuan quartet ruled so honestly that people stopped lying to one another.

sentences.zh: 王堂、陳寵委任賢良，而職事自理：斯皆可以感物而行化也。

translations.literal: Wang Tang and Chen Chong entrusted office to worthy men, and business ordered itself—these too could move things and carry transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tang and Chen Chong delegated to talent and let affairs run themselves—they too transformed their jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 邊鳳、延篤先後爲京兆尹，時人以辈前世趙、張。

translations.literal: Bian Feng and Yan Du successively served as metropolitan governor; men of the age bracketed them with the Zhao and Zhang of earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Feng and Yan Du, one after the other as governors of the capital, were likened to the legendary Zhao and Zhang of old.

sentences.zh: 又王渙、任峻之爲洛陽令，明發姦伏，吏端禁止，然導德劉禮，有所未充，亦一時之良能也。

translations.literal: Further Wang Huan and Ren Jun as magistrates of Luoyang laid bare hidden villainy; clerks stood straight and prohibitions held—yet in guiding virtue through ritual propriety something still fell short; still they were capable officers of their day.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan and Ren Jun as Luoyang magistrates exposed crime and kept clerks honest; moral instruction through ritual still fell short of the ideal, yet they ranked among the best of their time.

sentences.zh: 今綴集殊聞顯迹，以爲《循吏篇》云。

translations.literal: Now I string together unusual hearings and shining deeds to form this chapter titled "Chapter on Upright Officials" (Xunli pian).
translations.idiomatic: What follows gathers notable deeds into the chapter "Chapter on Upright Officials" (the Xunli pian).

sentences.zh: 衛颯傳

translations.literal: Section heading: Biography of Wei Sa.
translations.idiomatic: This section heading introduces the biography of Wei Sa.

sentences.zh: 衛颯字子產，河内修武人也。

translations.literal: Wei Sa, courtesy name Zichan, was a man of Xiuwu in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sa, styled Zichan, came from Xiuwu in Henei.

sentences.zh: 家貧好學問，隨師無粮，常佣以自給。

translations.literal: His family was poor yet he loved learning; following his teacher he had no grain and regularly hired himself out to supply his needs.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but devoted to books, he hired out as a laborer to buy lessons.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，仕郡历州宰。

translations.literal: Under Wang Mang he served the commandery, ascending through district magistrate posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang he rose from county posts in his commandery.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，辟大司徒鄧禹府。

translations.literal: In the second Jianwu year he was summoned to Grand Excellency Deng Yu’s bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 26 he entered Grand Excellency Deng Yu’s staff.

sentences.zh: 舉能案剧，除侍御史，襄城令。

translations.literal: Recommended able to handle knotty cases, he was appointed attendant censor and magistrate of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for handling tough litigation, he became attendant imperial secretary and magistrate of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 政有名迹，遷桂陽太守。

translations.literal: His administration left a notable record; he was promoted governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His record stood out; he was elevated to governor of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 郡与交州接境，頗染其俗，不知禮則。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered Jiao Province and had absorbed much of its custom, ignorant of ritual norms.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang touched Jiao Province and had picked up frontier habits light on ritual.

sentences.zh: 颯下車，修庠序之教，設婚姻之禮。

translations.literal: When Sa stepped down from his carriage he repaired school instruction and instituted marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he rebuilt schools and taught marriage etiquette.

sentences.zh: 期年間，邦俗從化。

translations.literal: Within a full year the commandery’s customs followed transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year local ways began to change.

sentences.zh: 先是，含洭、浈陽，曲江三縣，越之故地，武帝平之，内属桂陽。

translations.literal: Earlier the three counties of Hanqu, Zhenyang, and Qujiang had been Yue territory; Emperor Wu had conquered them and attached them to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqu, Zhenyang, and Qujiang had been Yue ground until Emperor Wu annexed them into Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 民居深山，濱溪谷，习其風土，不出田租。

translations.literal: The people dwelt deep in the hills along streams and gorges, accustomed to their soil and wind, and paid no field rent.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in mountain valleys and paid no grain tax, bound to old frontier habits.

sentences.zh: 去郡远者，或且千里。

translations.literal: Those farthest from the commandery seat might be nearly a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Some settlements lay nearly a thousand li from the yamen.

sentences.zh: 吏事徃 来，輒發民乘船，名曰“傳役”。

translations.literal: When clerks came and went they routinely drafted commoners to man boats, calling it “relay labor”.
translations.idiomatic: Official traffic drafted villagers onto boats as “relay duty”.

sentences.zh: 每一吏出，徭及數家，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Every time one clerk went out, corvée touched several households—the people suffered it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: One messenger could burden several families; the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 颯乃凿山通道五百餘里，列亭傳，置邮驿。

translations.literal: Sa then cut mountain passages over five hundred li, posting relay lodges and establishing courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sa carved roads five hundred li through the hills and built posts and relay stations.

sentences.zh: 于是役省劳息，姦吏杜絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon labor was spared and toil rested; corrupt clerks were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée fell silent and corrupt runners disappeared.

sentences.zh: 流民稍還，渐成聚邑，使输租賦，同之平民。

translations.literal: Wandering people gradually returned and slowly formed settlements; he made them render rent and tax like ordinary subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees drifted back, villages grew, and he taxed them like any Han farmer.

sentences.zh: 又耒陽縣出鐵石，佗郡民庶常依因聚會，私爲冶鑄，遂招来亡命，多致姦盗。

translations.literal: Further Leiyang county produced iron ore; commoners of other commanderies often gathered there by arrangement to smelt privately for casting, thereby attracting fugitives and breeding much banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Leiyang’s iron drew outsiders to illegal furnaces, fugitives, and bandits.

sentences.zh: 颯乃上起鐵官，罷斥私鑄，歲所增入五百餘萬。

translations.literal: Sa therefore petitioned to erect iron offices, abolish private casting—annual revenue rose by more than five million.
translations.idiomatic: He established government ironworks and banned private smelting, adding over five million cash a year.

sentences.zh: 颯 理恤民事，居官如家，其所施政，莫不合于物宜。

translations.literal: Sa managed and pitied the people’s affairs; holding office like managing a household—whatever he enacted suited circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the commandery like a household—every policy fit local conditions.

sentences.zh: 視事十年，郡内清理。

translations.literal: After ten years in office the interior of the commandery was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years Guiyang was orderly within.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，征還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: In 49 he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 光武欲以爲少府，會颯被疾，不能拜起，敕以桂陽太守歸家，須后詔書。

translations.literal: Guangwu wished to make him superintendent of the household; it happened that Sa fell ill and could not rise for appointment—an edict sent him home as governor of Guiyang to await later summons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to name him superintendent of the household, but illness kept him from rising for audience; he was ordered home as governor of Guiyang pending further edict.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，載病詣阙，自陳困篤，乃收印绶，賜錢十萬，后卒于家。

translations.literal: After two years he rode ill to the palace gates, stating his grave condition; his seals were taken, one hundred thousand cash granted, and later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he appeared at court dying; they stripped his seals, gave him one hundred thousand cash, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 南陽茨充代颯爲桂陽。

translations.literal: Ci Chong of Nanyang succeeded Sa as governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ci Chong of Nanyang replaced Wei Sa in Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 亦善其政，教民种殖桑柘麻紵之属，勸令養蠶織履，民得利益焉。

translations.literal: He too excelled in governance, teaching the people to plant mulberry, hemp, and ramie, urging them to rear silkworms and weave sandals—the people profited.
translations.idiomatic: Ci Chong taught mulberry, hemp, and weaving—sericulture and straw sandals—and the people gained.

sentences.zh: 任延字長孫，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: Ren Yan, courtesy name Zhangsun, was a man of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan, styled Zhangsun, came from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 年十二，爲諸生，學于長安，明《詩》、《易》、《春秋》，顯名太學，學中號爲“任圣童”。

translations.literal: At twelve sui he became a student, studying at Chang’an; he mastered the Odes, Changes, and Spring and Autumn Annals, gaining fame in the Imperial Academy—students there dubbed him “Saint Boy Ren.”
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he studied in Chang’an, mastering the Odes, Changes, and Spring and Autumn Annals, and the academy nicknamed him “the boy sage.”

sentences.zh: 值仓卒，避兵之陇西。

translations.literal: When crisis struck he fled the soldiers to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos erupted he fled to Longxi.

sentences.zh: 時隗嚣已據四郡，遣使請延，延不應。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Ao already held four commanderies and sent envoys to summon Yan—Yan did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ao offered him office over four commanderies; Ren Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 更始元年，以延爲大司馬属，拜會稽都尉。

translations.literal: In the first Gengshi year Yan was made aide to the grand marshal and appointed chief commandant of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In 23 he joined the Gengshi regime as grand marshal’s aide and chief commandant of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 時年十九，迎官驚其壮。

translations.literal: At nineteen sui the welcoming officials marveled at his youth.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen his arrival officers gasped at his age.

sentences.zh: 及到，靜泊無爲，唯先遣馈禮祠延陵季子。

translations.literal: When he arrived he remained quiet and inactive, first sending ritual offerings to sacrifice to Yanling Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: On landing he did nothing flashy—first he sacrificed to Yanling Jizi as ritual demanded.

sentences.zh: 時，天下新定，道路未通，避亂江南者皆未還中土，會稽頗稱多士。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had newly settled; roads were not yet open—those who had fled south in chaos had not returned to the central plain; Kuaiji was famed for many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The land was newly pacified and roads unsafe; refugees still crowded the south, and Kuaiji teemed with talent.

sentences.zh: 延到，皆聘請高行如董子儀、严子陵等，敬待以師友之禮。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived he engaged high-minded men such as Dong Ziyi and Yan Ziling, honoring them with teacher-and-friend courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan recruited Dong Ziyi, Yan Ziling, and other worthies as peers and mentors.

sentences.zh: 掾吏貧者，輒分奉禄以赈給之。

translations.literal: When clerks were poor he divided his salary to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He split his pay among needy clerks.

sentences.zh: 省諸卒，令耕公田，以周穷急。

translations.literal: He reduced garrison soldiers, ordering them to till public fields to relieve the desperate poor.
translations.idiomatic: He cut guardsmen and put them on public land to feed the destitute.

sentences.zh: 每時行縣，輒使慰勉孝子，就餐饭之。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured counties he sent men to comfort filial sons and shared meals with them.
translations.idiomatic: On circuit he sought out filial sons and broke bread with them.

sentences.zh: 吳有龙丘苌者，隱居太末，志不降辱。

translations.literal: There was Longqiu Chang of Wu, dwelling hidden at Taimo, resolved never to bow in humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Longqiu Chang of Wu hid at Taimo and would not demean himself.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，四輔三公連辟，不到。

translations.literal: Under Wang Mang the four adjuncts and three excellencies repeatedly summoned him—he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang’s chief ministers summoned him repeatedly—he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 掾史白請召之。

translations.literal: Clerks reported asking permission to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Staff asked leave to drag him in.

sentences.zh: 延曰：“龙丘先生躬德履義，有原憲、伯夷之節。

translations.literal: Yan said: “Sir Longqiu embodies virtue and walks in righteousness—he has the integrity of Yuan Xian and Boyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan answered: “Longqiu Chang matches Yuan Xian and Boyi in integrity."

sentences.zh: 都尉埽洒其門，犹惧辱焉，召之不可。

translations.literal: Were the chief commandant to sweep his gate he would still fear insult—summoning him will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I swept his doorstep I might insult him—do not summon."

sentences.zh: ”遣功曹奉谒，修書记，致醫藥，吏使相望于道。

translations.literal: ” He dispatched the merit assessor with visiting cards, letters, and medicines; runners and riders crowded the road.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the merit assessor with letters, gifts, and doctors—messengers crowded the road.

sentences.zh: 積一歲，苌乃乘辇詣府門，愿得先死备录。

translations.literal: After a full year Chang rode a litter to the commandery gate, wishing first to die then be enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Longqiu Chang rode to the gate and asked to register his service.

sentences.zh: 延辭讓再三，遂署議曹祭酒。

translations.literal: Yan declined repeatedly; finally he appointed him libationer of the deliberation bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan demurred, then named him deliberation libationer.

sentences.zh: 苌寻病卒，延自臨殡，不朝三日。

translations.literal: Chang soon died of illness; Yan personally attended the funeral and did not hold court three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Longqiu Chang died Ren Yan buried him himself and suspended audience three days.

sentences.zh: 是以郡中賢士大夫爭徃 宦焉。

translations.literal: Therefore worthy gentlemen of the commandery vied to enter his service.
translations.idiomatic: Notables then competed for posts under him.

sentences.zh: 建武初，延上書愿乞骸骨，歸拜王庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu Yan memorialized begging to surrender his bones and return to audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu he asked leave to retire and report at court.

sentences.zh: 詔征爲九真太守。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him as governor of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him governor of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 光武引見，賜馬杂缯，令妻子留洛陽。

translations.literal: Guangwu granted him audience, bestowed horses and silks, and ordered wife and children to remain at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu received him, gave horses and silk, and kept his family hostage at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九真俗以謝獵爲業，不知牛耕，民常告籴交阯，每致困乏。

translations.literal: Jiuzhen custom took slash-and-burn hunting as livelihood; they did not know ox plowing—commoners constantly bought grain from Jiaozhi and often fell into want.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen lived by swidden hunting and knew no plow oxen; they bought grain from Jiaozhi and often starved.

sentences.zh: 延乃令鑄作田器，教之垦辟。

translations.literal: Yan then ordered farm tools cast and taught them to clear land.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan had iron tools forged and taught wet-field farming.

sentences.zh: 田畴歲歲开廣，百姓充給。

translations.literal: Fields opened wider year by year; the common people had enough.
translations.idiomatic: Each year more land opened and bellies filled.

sentences.zh: 又骆越之民無嫁娶禮法，各因淫好，無適對匹，不識父子之性，夫婦之道。

translations.literal: Further the Luo Yue people had no marriage ritual—each followed lustful fancy without proper pairing, knowing neither the nature of father and son nor the way of husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo Yue had no marriage law—liaisons were casual, kinship murky.

sentences.zh: 延乃移書属縣，各使男年二十至五十，女年十五至四十，皆以年齿相配。

translations.literal: Yan then sent orders to the counties: let males aged twenty to fifty and females fifteen to forty pair by age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered county males twenty to fifty and females fifteen to forty matched by age.

sentences.zh: 其貧無禮娉，令長吏以下各省奉禄以赈助之。

translations.literal: Those too poor for bride-price—magistrates down were each to trim salary to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Poor couples received subsidies from official salaries.

sentences.zh: 同時相娶者二千餘人。

translations.literal: More than two thousand married at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Over two thousand wed in one wave.

sentences.zh: 是歲風雨順節，谷稼豐衍。

translations.literal: That year wind and rain kept season; grain crops flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Rain came on time and harvests swelled.

sentences.zh: 其產子者，始知种姓。

translations.literal: Those who bore children then knew lineage and surname.
translations.idiomatic: Parents finally traced clan names for their children.

sentences.zh: 咸曰：“使我有是子者，任君也。

translations.literal: All said: “It is Prefect Ren who gave me this child.
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Prefect Ren gave us these children."

sentences.zh: ”多名子爲“任”。

translations.literal: ” Many named sons “Ren”.
translations.idiomatic: Many boys received the given name Ren.

sentences.zh: 于是徼外蛮夷夜郎等慕義保塞，延遂止罷侦候戍卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon barbarians beyond the pale such as Yelang admired righteousness and guarded the passes—Yan then ceased frontier scouts and garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yelang and other tribes pledged loyalty; Ren Yan stood down scouts and border guards.

sentences.zh: 初，平帝時，漢中錫光爲交阯太守，教導民夷，渐以禮義，化聲侔于延。

translations.literal: Earlier, under Emperor Ping, Xi Guang of Hanzhong had been governor of Jiaozhi, instructing commoners and tribes in gradual ritual—his transforming fame matched Yan’s.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi Guang of Hanzhong had governed Jiaozhi under Emperor Ping with the same civilizing fame.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，閉境拒守。

translations.literal: At Wang Mang’s end he closed the borders and held defense.
translations.idiomatic: At Wang Mang’s fall he sealed his frontier.

sentences.zh: 建武初，遣使贡獻，封盐水侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he sent tribute and was enfeoffed marquis of Yanshui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu he submitted tribute and became marquis of Yanshui.

sentences.zh: 领南华風，始于二守焉。

translations.literal: The southern frontier’s embrace of Central Plains polish began with these two governors.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing influence in the deep south began with these two governors.

sentences.zh: 延視事四年，征詣洛陽，以病稽留，左轉睢陽令，九真吏人生爲立祠。

translations.literal: After four years in office Yan was summoned to Luoyang; detained by illness he was shifted left to magistrate of Suiyang—the officials and people of Jiuzhen raised a shrine to him while he lived.
translations.idiomatic: After four years illness delayed him at Luoyang; demoted to Suiyang magistrate, Jiuzhen built him a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 拜武威太守，帝亲見，戒之曰：“善事上官，無失名誉。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Wuwei; the emperor personally received him and admonished: “Serve your superiors well—do not ruin your reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Named Wuwei governor, the emperor warned him to curry favor with superiors.

sentences.zh: ”延對曰：“臣聞忠臣不私，私臣不忠。

translations.literal: ” Yan replied: “Your servant has heard that loyal ministers are not private; private ministers are not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan answered: "Loyal ministers are never cronies; cronies are never loyal."

sentences.zh: 履正奉公，臣子之節。

translations.literal: Walking the straight path and upholding the public good is the duty of minister and son.
translations.idiomatic: Impartial service is a minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 上下雷同，非陛下之福。

translations.literal: High and low echoing each other alike is not Your Majesty’s blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Yes-men echoing one another help no throne.

sentences.zh: 善事上官，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: To serve superiors well—your servant dares not receive such an edict.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot obey an order to flatter bosses.

sentences.zh: ”帝嘆息曰：“卿言是也。

translations.literal: ” The emperor sighed: “What you say is right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "You speak truth."

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark ending the emperor’s remark.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s approving reply ends here.

sentences.zh: 既之武威，時將兵長史田紺，郡之大姓，其子弟賓客爲人暴害。

translations.literal: Once he reached Wuwei, at that time Colonel Director of Troops Tian Gan of the commandery, a great clan—his sons and retainers tyrannized others.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuwei Colonel Tian Gan’s clan bullied the people.

sentences.zh: 延收紺系之，父子賓客伏法者五六人。

translations.literal: Yan seized Gan and bound him; fathers, sons, and retainers who suffered execution numbered five or six.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan arrested Tian Gan and executed five or six kin and clients.

sentences.zh: 紺少子尚乃聚會輕薄數百人，自號將軍，夜来攻郡。

translations.literal: Gan’s youngest son Shang then gathered several hundred rowdies, styled himself general, and attacked the commandery by night.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shang rallied hundreds of ruffians, called himself general, and struck the yamen by night.

sentences.zh: 延即發兵破之。

translations.literal: Yan immediately raised troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan attacked at once and broke Tian Shang's rising.

sentences.zh: 自是威行境内，吏民累息。

translations.literal: From this his awesome authority ran through the interior; clerks and commoners breathed easier again and again.
translations.idiomatic: His grip on the commandery tightened and the people finally rested.

sentences.zh: 郡北當匈奴，南接种羌，民畏寇抄，多廢田業。

translations.literal: North the commandery faced the Xiongnu; south it adjoined dependent Qiang—the people feared raiders and abandoned many fields.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiongnu to the north and Qiang to the south, raids emptied the farms.

sentences.zh: 延到，选集武略之士千人，明其賞罰，令將杂种胡騎休屠黄石屯據要害，其有警急，逆擊追討。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived he selected a thousand men skilled in arms, clarified rewards and punishments, and ordered miscellaneous Hu horsemen from the Xiutu Huangshi garrison to hold choke points—when alarms came they counterstruck and pursued.
translations.idiomatic: He picked a thousand fighters, set clear rewards, and posted Xiutu auxiliaries on the passes to ambush raiders.

sentences.zh: 虏恒多残傷，遂絕不敢出。

translations.literal: The enemy constantly suffered many killed and wounded; finally they dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated losses the nomads stopped venturing out.

sentences.zh: 河西旧少雨澤，乃爲置水官吏，修理沟渠，皆蒙其利。

translations.literal: West of the River had long seen little rain—he therefore appointed water officers, repaired ditches and canals, and all benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned irrigation officers and dredged channels across the arid Hexi corridor.

sentences.zh: 又造立校官，自掾史子孫，皆令詣學受業，复其徭役。

translations.literal: Further he founded school officers—clerks' sons and grandsons were all ordered to attend school and study; their corvée was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He founded official schools, sent clerks' children to class, and excused them from labor duty.

sentences.zh: 章句既通。

translations.literal: Once gloss and verse were mastered.
translations.idiomatic: When they had mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 悉顯拔荣進之。

translations.literal: He promoted them all for glory and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted every graduate who proved worthy.

sentences.zh: 郡遂有儒雅之士。

translations.literal: The commandery then had scholarly gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly talent began to flourish there.

sentences.zh: 后坐擅诛羌不先上，左轉召陵令。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached for executing Qiang without prior memorial—he was shifted left to magistrate of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He lost rank for killing Qiang without imperial leave and became magistrate of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 顯宗即位，拜潁川太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended he was appointed governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed him governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 永平二年，征會辟雍，因以爲河内太守。

translations.literal: In the second Yongping year he was summoned to the Hall of the Circular Moat and thereupon made governor of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In 59 he attended the Biyong academy and was named governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 視事九年，病卒。

translations.literal: After nine years in office he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office after nine years.

sentences.zh: 少子恺，官至太常。

translations.literal: The youngest son Kai rose to minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Ren Kai became minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 王景字仲通，乐浪讲邯人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, courtesy name Zhongtong, was a man of Jiang district in Lelang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing, styled Zhongtong, came from Lelang.

sentences.zh: 八世祖仲，本琅邪不其人。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhong was originally a native of Buqi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back the clan came from Buqi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 好道术，明天文。

translations.literal: He loved Daoist arts and understood astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestor practiced esoteric arts and read the stars.

sentences.zh: 諸吕作亂，劉哀王襄谋發兵，而數問于仲。

translations.literal: When the Lü clan made turmoil Prince Ai of Liu plotted to raise troops and repeatedly questioned Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Lü coup Prince Liu Xiang consulted Zhong about raising troops.

sentences.zh: 及济北王興居反，欲委兵師仲，仲惧祸及，乃浮海東奔乐浪山中，因而家焉。

translations.literal: When the prince of Jibei Xingju rebelled he wished to entrust troops to Zhong as teacher—Zhong feared calamity reaching him and fled east across the sea to the Lelang hills, where the family settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xingju revolted he tried to drag Zhong into the war; Zhong fled by sea to Lelang and stayed.

sentences.zh: 父閎，爲郡三老。

translations.literal: His father Hong served as village elder of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Hong was a commandery elder.

sentences.zh: 更始敗，土人王調殺郡守劉憲，自稱大將軍、乐浪太守。

translations.literal: When the Gengshi regime collapsed local Wang Diao killed Inspector Liu Xian, styling himself grand general and governor of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: After Gengshi fell, Wang Diao murdered the inspector and seized Lelang.

sentences.zh: 建武六年，光武遣太守王遵將兵擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth Jianwu year Guangwu dispatched Governor Wang Zun with troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In 30 Emperor Guangwu sent Wang Zun to crush the rebel.

sentences.zh: 至遼東，閎与郡决曹史杨邑等共殺調迎遵，皆封爲列侯，閎独讓爵。

translations.literal: Reaching Liaodong, Hong together with commandery clerk Yang Yi and others jointly killed Diao and welcomed Zun—all were enfeoffed as full marquises; Hong alone declined the title.
translations.idiomatic: Near Liaodong Wang Hong and Yang Yi killed Wang Diao and welcomed Wang Zun—everyone gained a marquisate except Wang Hong, who refused.

sentences.zh: 帝奇而征之，道病座。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled and summoned him—he fell ill en route and died.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Wang Hong, but he died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 景少學《易》，遂廣窺衆書，又好天文术數之事，沈深多伎艺。

translations.literal: Jing in youth studied the Book of Changes, broadly surveyed many writings, and loved astronomy and numerology—profound and skilled in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing mastered the Changes, read widely, and delved into astrology and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 辟司空伏恭府。

translations.literal: He was summoned to Minister of Works Fu Gong's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Minister of Works Fu Gong's staff.

sentences.zh: 時有薦景能理水者，顯宗詔与將作谒者王吳共修作浚儀渠。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Jing could manage water—Emperor Xiaozong ordered him with Director of Works herald Wang Wu jointly to repair the Junyi canal.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for hydraulic skill, he rebuilt the Junyi canal with Wang Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳用景墕流法，水乃不复爲害。

translations.literal: Wu used Jing's flow-dividing method—the water no longer harmed fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu applied Wang Jing's channel scheme and ended the flooding.

sentences.zh: 初，平帝時，河、汴决壞，未及得修。

translations.literal: Earlier, under Emperor Ping, the Yellow River and Bian Canal had burst—there had been no chance to repair.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Ping the Yellow River and Bian had broken their banks unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 建武十年，陽武令張汜上言：“河决積久，日月侵毁，济渠所漂數十許縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth Jianwu year Yangwu Magistrate Zhang Fan memorialized: "The river breach has lasted long—day by day it eats away—the Ji canal has flooded dozens of counties.
translations.idiomatic: In 34 Zhang Fan of Yangwu warned that the breach was washing away dozens of counties along the Ji canal.

sentences.zh: 修理之费，其功不難。

translations.literal: The cost of repair—the achievement is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Fixing it would not be impossible.

sentences.zh: 宜改修堤防，以安百姓。

translations.literal: We ought to rebuild dikes to settle the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring levees for the farmers.

sentences.zh: ”書奏，光武即爲發卒。

translations.literal: " The memorial submitted—Guangwu immediately drafted soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu mobilized labor on reading the memorial.

sentences.zh: 方营河功，而逡儀令乐俊复上言：“昔元光之間，人庶炽盛，缘堤垦殖，而瓠子河决，尚二十餘年，不即拥塞。

translations.literal: Just as river works were underway Junyi Magistrate Le Jun again memorialized: "Formerly between the Yuanguang years population was dense—along dikes they opened fields—when Huzi breached it still took twenty years before it could be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Then Junyi's Le Jun argued that even Han Wudi needed decades to plug Huzi.

sentences.zh: 今居家稀少，田地饒廣，雖未修理，其患犹可。

translations.literal: Now households are sparse and fields wide—even without repair the peril is still tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer people and open land, he said the flood risk was bearable for now.

sentences.zh: 且新被兵革，方興役力，劳怨既多，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Moreover we are newly scarred by war—if we raise labor now bitterness and resentment multiply—the people cannot bear the command.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from war, another giant corvée would spark revolt.

sentences.zh: 宜須平靜，更議其事。

translations.literal: We should wait for calm and revisit the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to postpone dikes until peace returned.

sentences.zh: ”光武得此遂止。

translations.literal: " Guangwu received this and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu shelved the project.

sentences.zh: 后汴渠東侵，日月彌廣，而水門故處，皆在河中，兗、豫百姓怨嘆，以爲縣官恒興佗役，不先民急。

translations.literal: Later the Bian canal eroded eastward daily wider—old water gates all lay midstream—Yan and Yu people complained that the court always raised other projects before their urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Bian overwhelmed its gates; Yan and Yu farmers accused the court of ignoring their floods.

sentences.zh: 永平十二年，議修汴渠，乃引見景，問以理水形便。

translations.literal: In the twelfth Yongping year they debated repairing the Bian canal—summoned Jing and asked him the lay of water control.
translations.idiomatic: In 69 the court consulted Wang Jing on rebuilding the Yellow River–Bian works.

sentences.zh: 景陳其利害，應對敏給，帝善之。

translations.literal: Jing laid out advantages and harms—answers quick and fluent—the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He explained hydraulics cogently and won the emperor's trust.

sentences.zh: 又以嘗修浚儀，功業有成，乃賜景《山海經》、《河渠書》、《禹贡图》及錢帛衣物。

translations.literal: Because he had repaired Junyi successfully—bestowed the Classic of Mountains and Seas, River Works, Yu tribute map, plus cash, silk, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: For his Junyi success the emperor gave him reference texts, maps, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 夏，遂發卒數十萬，遣景与王吳修渠筑堤，自荥陽東至千乘海口千餘里。

translations.literal: That summer they drafted tens of thousands of laborers—sent Jing and Wang Wu to dig the canal and build dikes—from Xingyang east to the Qiansheng estuary over a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: That summer tens of thousands dug from Xingyang to the sea.

sentences.zh: 景乃商度地勢，凿山阜，破砥績，直截沟涧，防遏冲要，疏决壅積，十里立一水門，令更相洄注，無复潰漏之患。

translations.literal: Jing surveyed terrain—cut hills, broke rock shoals, bridged gullies, blocked choke points, dredged jams—every ten li one water gate—alternating backflow—no more breach leaks.
translations.idiomatic: He engineered gates, cuts, and spillways so the river could bleed pressure without jumping its banks.

sentences.zh: 景雖简省役费，然犹以百亿计。

translations.literal: Though Jing economized on labor and expense, still the cost ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Even trimmed, the project cost hundreds of millions of cash.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，渠成。

translations.literal: The next summer the canal was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The channel opened the following summer.

sentences.zh: 帝亲自巡行，詔濱河郡國置河堤員吏，如西京旧制。

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured—ordered riverbank commanderies and kingdoms to appoint river-dike clerks—like the western capital's old system.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inspected the line and restored Eastern Han's river inspectors.

sentences.zh: 景由是知名。

translations.literal: Jing became famous thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing's name spread empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 王吳及諸從事掾史皆增秩一等。

translations.literal: Wang Wu and all clerk aides were promoted one salary grade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu and the engineering staff each gained a rank.

sentences.zh: 景三遷爲侍御史。

translations.literal: Jing was thrice promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing rose thrice to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從駕車巡狩，至無盐，帝美其功績，拜河堤谒者，賜車馬缣錢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the imperial carriage on tour—to Wuyan—the emperor praised his merit—appointed herald of river dikes—bestowed carriage, horses, silk, and cash.
translations.idiomatic: On the 72 hunt he received the river-herald post and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 建初七年，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh Jianchu year he was promoted inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In 82 he became inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 先是杜陵杜篤奏上《論都賦》，欲令車駕遷還長安。

translations.literal: Earlier Du Ling's Du Du submitted the Rhapsody on the Capital—wishing the imperial carriage would return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Du Du's poem had stirred nostalgia for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 耆老聞者，皆動懷土之心，莫不眷然伫立西望。

translations.literal: Elders who heard were all moved with longing for home—none failed to stand yearning west.
translations.idiomatic: Older listeners pined for the old western capital.

sentences.zh: 景以宫廟已立，恐人情疑惑，會時有神雀諸瑞，乃作《金人論》，頌洛邑之美，天人之符，文有可采。

translations.literal: Jing thought palace temples already stood at Luoyang—feared popular doubt—when divine sparrows and other omens appeared—composed the Discourse on Golden Men praising Luoyang's beauty and heaven's signs—the text had passages worth citing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing defended Luoyang in his Discourse on Golden Men, citing omens to steady opinion.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷庐江太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted governor of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he governed Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 先是，百姓不知牛耕，致地力有余而食常不足。

translations.literal: Earlier the commoners did not know ox plowing—land strength lay surplus yet food was often insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: There farmers still relied on swidden; yields lagged despite rich soil.

sentences.zh: 郡界有楚相孫叔敖所起芍陂稻田。

translations.literal: Within the commandery lay the paddy of Shaopi marsh that Chu minister Sun Shuao had built.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shuao's ancient Shaopi reservoir still watered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 景乃驅率吏民，修起蕪廢，教用犁耕，由是垦辟倍多，境内豐給。

translations.literal: Jing drove clerks and people—restored ruined works—taught plow farming—thereupon reclaimed land more than doubled—the interior became abundantly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Shaopi, taught iron plows, and doubled the cleared acreage.

sentences.zh: 遂铭石刻誓，令民知常禁。

translations.literal: Then he inscribed stone oaths—let the people know standing prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: He carved regulations in stone so farmers knew the rules.

sentences.zh: 又训令蠶織，爲作法制，皆著于乡亭，庐江傳其文辭。

translations.literal: Further he instructed silkworm rearing and weaving—made regulations—all posted at rural posts—Lujiang transmitted his texts.
translations.idiomatic: He issued sericulture rules posted at every pavilion.

sentences.zh: 卒于官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 初，景以爲《六經》所載，皆有卜筮，作事舉止，質于蓍龟，而衆書错糅，吉凶相反，乃参纪衆家數术文書，冢宅禁忌，堪舆日相之属，適于事用者，集爲《大衍玄基》云。

translations.literal: Earlier Jing thought the Six Classics all record divination—undertaking affairs must be referred to milfoil and tortoise—but the many books were jumbled—good and ill reversed—thereupon he collated various schools' numerology writings, tomb and dwelling taboos, geomancy and day-selection—whatever suited practice—and collected them into the Dayan Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled mantic texts into the Dayan Xuanji, trying to harmonize conflicting omens.

sentences.zh: 秦袁字伯平，扶風茂陵人也。

translations.literal: Qin Yuan, courtesy name Boping, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yuan, styled Boping, came from Maoling in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 自漢興之后，世位相承。

translations.literal: Since Han rose the generations had held office in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration his clan held posts generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 六世祖袭，爲潁川太守，与群從同時爲二千石者五人，故三輔號曰“萬石秦氏”。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Xi was governor of Yingchuan—with cousins five men simultaneously at two thousand shi salary—therefore the Three Adjuncts titled them the "Ten-Thousand-Shi Qin clan."
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back five Qins held two-thousand-shi posts—hence the "ten-thousand-shi Qins."

sentences.zh: 彭同產女弟，顯宗時入掖庭爲貴人，有寵。

translations.literal: Peng's younger sister by the same mother entered the rear palace as an honored lady in the Xiaozong era—she was favored.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Peng's sister became a favored consort under Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 永平七年，以彭貴人兄，隨四姓小侯擢爲开陽城門候。

translations.literal: In the seventh Yongping year, as elder brother of Honored Lady Qin, he was raised with the four-surname minor marquises to guard the Kaiyang city gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 64, as the imperial consort's brother, he joined the lesser marquises guarding Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜騎都尉，副驸馬都尉耿秉北征匈奴。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed colonel of cavalry—deputy to Colonel of Carriage and Cavalry Geng Bing on the northern expedition against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: In 72 he rode north as colonel of cavalry beside Geng Bing.

sentences.zh: 建初元年，遷山陽太守。

translations.literal: In the first Jianchu year he was promoted governor of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 76 he became governor of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 以禮训人，不任刑罰。

translations.literal: He instructed people with ritual—did not rely on punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled through ritual education, not the lash.

sentences.zh: 崇好儒雅，敦明庠序。

translations.literal: He esteemed scholars—promoted schools.
translations.idiomatic: He championed Confucian schools.

sentences.zh: 每春秋飨射，輒修升降揖讓之儀。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn communal feast and archery—he always practiced the ascending, descending, bowing, and yielding rites.
translations.idiomatic: At village archery feasts he drilled bowing and yielding etiquette.

sentences.zh: 乃爲人設四诫，以定六亲長幼之禮。

translations.literal: He established four admonitions for the people—fixing ritual between the six kin old and young.
translations.idiomatic: He issued four village rules to sort kinship duties.

sentences.zh: 有遵奉教化者，擢爲乡三老，常以八月致酒肉以勸勉之。

translations.literal: Those who obeyed his teaching—he promoted as village elders—each eighth month sent wine and meat to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Obedient villages gained elders rewarded with autumn wine.

sentences.zh: 吏有過咎，罷遣而已，不加耻辱。

translations.literal: Clerks who faulted—he dismissed only—added no shame punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Erring clerks were simply removed, not humiliated.

sentences.zh: 百姓懷爱，莫有欺犯。

translations.literal: The common people cherished him—none deceived or offended.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him and stopped cheating.

sentences.zh: 興起稻田數千頃，每于农月，亲度頃亩，分别肥瘠，差爲三品，各立文簿，藏之乡縣。

translations.literal: He raised paddy fields numbering thousands of qing—each farming month he personally surveyed acres—divided fertile from lean—three grades—each established registers—stored in county offices.
translations.idiomatic: He classified every plot into three fertility grades in county registers.

sentences.zh: 于是姦吏跼蹐，無所容詐。

translations.literal: Thereupon corrupt clerks cowered—had nowhere to cheat.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt registrars could no longer hide fertile land.

sentences.zh: 彭乃上言，宜令天下劉同其制。

translations.literal: Peng memorialized—should order the empire to adopt his system.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Peng urged making his land survey a national model.

sentences.zh: 詔書以其所立条式，班令三府，並下州郡。

translations.literal: An edict took the regulations he established—issued them through the Three Offices—and sent them down to provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The court promulgated his forms through the Three Ducal Offices.

sentences.zh: 在職六年，轉潁川太守，仍有鳳皇、麒麟、嘉禾、甘露之瑞，集其郡境。

translations.literal: After six years in office he was transferred governor of Yingchuan—phoenix, qilin, auspicious grain, and sweet dew omens gathered within the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later Yingchuan showered him with omens.

sentences.zh: 肅宗巡行，再幸潁川，輒賞賜錢谷，恩寵甚異。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong on tour twice favored Yingchuan—always gifted cash and grain—grace was exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang visited twice and heaped rewards on him.

sentences.zh: 章和二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second Zhanghe year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 88.

sentences.zh: 鼓弟惇、褒，並爲射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Gu's younger brothers Dun and Bao—both colonels of the sound of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Qin Dun and Qin Bao became colonels of the sound of arrows.

sentences.zh: 王渙字稚子，廣漢郪人也。

translations.literal: Wang Huan, courtesy name Zhizi, was a man of Qi in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, styled Zhizi, came from Qi in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 父順，安定太守。

translations.literal: His father Shun was governor of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Shun governed Anding.

sentences.zh: 渙少好俠，尚氣力，數通剽輕少年。

translations.literal: Huan in youth loved knight-errantry—valued strength—often mixed with reckless youths.
translations.idiomatic: Young Wang Huan swaggered with swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 晚而改節，敦儒學，习《尚書》，读律令，略舉大義。

translations.literal: Later he reformed—embraced Confucian learning—studied the Book of Documents—read statutes—grasped the main principles.
translations.idiomatic: He sobered up, turned to the Documents and Han law.

sentences.zh: 爲太守陳寵功曹，當職割断，不避豪右。

translations.literal: He served Governor Chen Chong as merit assessor—when on duty he decided decisively—not avoiding the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Chong's merit assessor he faced down magnates.

sentences.zh: 寵風聲大行，入爲大司农。

translations.literal: Chong's reputation spread greatly—entered as minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chong's fame carried him to minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 和帝問曰：“在郡何以爲理？

translations.literal: Emperor He asked: "In the commandery how did you govern?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He asked Chen Chong how he ruled.

sentences.zh: ”寵頓首謝曰：“臣任功曹王渙以简賢选能，主簿镡顯拾遺补阙，臣奉宣詔書而已。

translations.literal: " Chong bowed his head and replied: "Your servant employed Merit Assessor Wang Huan to select worthy talent—Chief Registrar Tan Xian picked up omissions—your servant merely conveyed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chong credited Wang Huan and Tan Xian and called himself only a messenger.

sentences.zh: ”帝大悦，渙由此顯名。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased—Huan thereby became famed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted and Wang Huan's name spread.

sentences.zh: 州舉茂才，除温令。

translations.literal: The province recommended him flourishing talent—appointed magistrate of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a flourishing talent, he became magistrate of Wen.

sentences.zh: 縣多姦猾，積爲人患。

translations.literal: The county had many crafty villains—long accumulated as the people's scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Wen county swarmed with predators.

sentences.zh: 渙以方略討擊，悉诛之。

translations.literal: Huan by stratagem attacked and struck—executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan extirpated them by design.

sentences.zh: 境内清夷，商人露宿于道。

translations.literal: The interior became clear—merchants slept exposed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Trade routes grew so safe merchants slept beside the road.

sentences.zh: 其有放牛者，輒云以属稚子，終無侵犯。

translations.literal: Those herding cattle always said they belonged to Zhizi—never were they violated.
translations.idiomatic: Herders simply said the herd belonged to Wang Huan and went unharmed.

sentences.zh: 在温三年，遷兗州刺史，绳正部郡，風威大行。

translations.literal: After three years at Wen he was promoted inspector of Yan Province—straightening subordinate commanderies—his majesty spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: Three years at Wen won him the Yan Province inspectorship and a reputation for stern fairness.

sentences.zh: 后坐考妖言不實論。

translations.literal: Later because investigation of occult speech proved untrue he was sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell under sentence when a sorcery probe collapsed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，征拜侍御史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was back as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 永元十五年，從駕南巡，還爲洛陽令。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth Yongyuan year he accompanied the southern tour—returned as magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 103 he rode the southern tour, then became Luoyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 以平正居身，得寬猛之宜。

translations.literal: He kept himself level and fair—achieving the balance of lenience and severity.
translations.idiomatic: He balanced mercy and rigor with impartial bearing.

sentences.zh: 其冤嫌久訟，历政所不断，法理所難平者，莫不曲盡情詐，压塞群疑。

translations.literal: Those grievances long litigated—what successive administrations could not decide—what principle could hardly settle—none failed to exhaust deceit and suppress crowd doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He settled suits deadlocked for years—every knot of fraud unraveled.

sentences.zh: 又能以谲數發□姦伏。

translations.literal: Further he could by subtle stratagem expose hidden villainy.
translations.idiomatic: Stratagem smoke-outs revealed hidden crime.

sentences.zh: 京師稱嘆，以爲渙有神算。

translations.literal: The capital praised him—thinking Huan had divine calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang whispered that Wang Huan read minds.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，病卒。

translations.literal: In the first Yuanxing year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 105.

sentences.zh: 百姓市道莫不咨嗟。

translations.literal: Market and street—none failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Every stall and lane mourned him.

sentences.zh: 男女老壮皆相与賦敛，致奠醊以千數。

translations.literal: Men and women old and strong together collected donations—libation offerings numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens pooled thousands of cups for his funeral wine.

sentences.zh: 渙丧西歸，道經弘农，民庶皆設槃桉于路。

translations.literal: Huan's bier went west—passing through Hongnong—commoners set trays along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Westbound through Hongnong, mourners lined his route with food.

sentences.zh: 吏問其故，咸言平常持米到洛，爲卒司所抄，恒亡其半。

translations.literal: Clerks asked the reason—all said ordinarily carrying grain to Luoyang—soldier clerks seized half—always losing half.
translations.idiomatic: They explained that grain convoys to Luoyang once lost half to rapacious guards.

sentences.zh: 自王君在事，不見侵枉，故来报恩。

translations.literal: Since Lord Wang held office—they saw no bullying—therefore they came to repay kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Huan the shakedowns stopped—this was their thanks.

sentences.zh: 其政化懷物如此。

translations.literal: His transformative embrace of things was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the loyalty his rule inspired.

sentences.zh: 民思其德，爲立祠安陽亭西，每食輒弦歌而薦之。

translations.literal: The people missed his virtue—raised a shrine west of Anyang pavilion—each meal they strummed and sang offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They built a shrine west of Anyang and sang him offerings at every meal.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，鄧太后詔曰：“夫忠良之吏，國家所以爲理也。

translations.literal: In the second Yongchu year Empress Dowager Deng decreed: "Loyal good officers—what the state relies on to govern.
translations.idiomatic: In 108 Empress Deng declared that honest magistrates anchored the realm.

sentences.zh: 求之甚勤，得之至寡。

translations.literal: You seek them very diligently—you obtain very few.
translations.idiomatic: They are hunted tirelessly yet rarely found.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：‘才難不其然乎！

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: Talent is hard—is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius called talent scarce.

sentences.zh: ’莫大司农朱邑、右扶風尹翁歸，政迹茂異，令名顯聞，孝宣皇帝嘉嘆悯惜，而以黄金百斤策賜其子。

translations.literal: " Never greater than Minister of Agriculture Zhu Yi and Governor of Youfufeng Yin Wenggui—their administrative traces splendidly unusual—their fair names famously heard—Emperor Xiaoxuan praised and pitied—bestowing one hundred jin of gold edict on their sons.
translations.idiomatic: She cited Zhu Yi and Yin Wenggui—Han Xuandi's rewarded ministers—as precedents.

sentences.zh: 故洛陽令王渙，秉清修之節，蹈羔羊之義，盡心奉公，務在惠民，功業未遂，不幸早世，百姓追思，爲之立祠。

translations.literal: Therefore Luoyang Magistrate Wang Huan—holding pure cultivation's integrity—treading the Lamb's righteousness—devoting heart to public good—aiming to benefit the people—merit unfinished—unfortunately died young—the common people pursued memory—raised a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: She praised Wang Huan's purity and the shrine citizens raised.

sentences.zh: 自非忠爱之至，孰能若斯者乎！

translations.literal: Had he not reached utmost loyalty and love—who could be like this!
translations.idiomatic: Only supreme devotion wins such grief.

sentences.zh: 今以渙子石爲郎中，以勸劳勤。

translations.literal: Now appoint Huan's son Shi gentleman of the palace—to encourage diligent service.
translations.idiomatic: She named Wang Shi a court gentleman to honor the dead father.

sentences.zh: ”延熹中，桓帝事黄、老道，悉毁諸房祀，唯特詔密縣存故太傅卓茂廟，洛陽留王渙祠焉。

translations.literal: " In the Yanxi era Emperor Huan practiced Huang-Lao Daoism—destroyed most rural shrines—only specially decreed Mi county keep former Grand Tutor Zhu Mao's temple—Luoyang retained Wang Huan's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Huan smashed local cults but spared Zhu Mao's shrine and Wang Huan's.

sentences.zh: 镡顯后亦知名，安帝時爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Tan Xian later also became famed—under Emperor An he was inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xian rose to Yu inspector under Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 時，天下飢荒，競爲盗贼，州界收捕且萬餘人。

translations.literal: At that time the realm suffered famine—men turned bandit—the province arrested nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Famine drove thousands into Tan Xian's nets.

sentences.zh: 顯愍其困穷，自陷刑辟，輒擅赦之，因自劾奏。

translations.literal: Xian pitied their destitution—self-trapped in crime—thereupon on his own authority pardoned them—then memorialized self-impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: He pitied starving thieves, freed them, then impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 有詔勿理。

translations.literal: An edict ordered no prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: The court forgave him.

sentences.zh: 后位至長乐衛尉。

translations.literal: Later he rose to colonel of the guards at Changle palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as colonel of the Changle guards.

sentences.zh: 自渙卒后，連詔三公特选洛陽令，皆不稱職。

translations.literal: Since Huan died—successive edicts ordered the Three Ducal Offices specially select Luoyang magistrate—none proved competent.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Huan died Luoyang magistrates disappointed every pick.

sentences.zh: 永和中，以剧令勃海任峻补之。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era—Ren Jun of Bohai—a county deemed knotty—filled the post.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghe Ren Jun of Bohai took the posting.

sentences.zh: 峻擢用文武吏，皆盡其能，纠剔姦盗，不得旋踵，一歲断狱，不過數十，威風猛于渙，而文理不及之。

translations.literal: Jun promoted civil and military clerks—each to full ability—purged bandits—before they could pivot—within one year settled cases—no more than several tens—awesome wind fiercer than Huan—but pattern and principle did not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Jun was sterner than Wang Huan but less subtle—few dozen cases a year yet fierce.

sentences.zh: 峻字叔高，終于太山太守。

translations.literal: Jun courtesy name Shugao—ended as governor of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Jun, styled Shugao, died as Taishan governor.

sentences.zh: 許荆字少張，會稽陽羡人也。

translations.literal: Xu Jing, courtesy name Shaozhang, was a man of Yangxian in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing, styled Shaozhang, came from Yangxian in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖父武，太守第五倫舉爲孝廉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wu—Governor Di Lun recommended him filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Xu Wu earned Di Lun's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 武以二弟晏、普未顯，欲令成名，乃請之曰：“禮有分異之義，家有别居之道。

translations.literal: Wu because two younger brothers Yan and Pu had not yet risen—wished them to win fame—therefore addressed them: "Ritual speaks of dividing households—family law allows separate dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: To launch his brothers' careers Xu Wu proposed splitting the estate.

sentences.zh: ”于是共割財產以爲三分，武自取肥田廣宅奴婢强者，二弟所得並悉劣少。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together they carved property into three shares—Wu himself took fertile fields, broad houses, strong slaves—the two brothers' portions were both inferior and small.
translations.idiomatic: He grabbed the best land and servants while short-changing Yan and Pu.

sentences.zh: 乡人皆稱弟克讓而鄙武貪婪，晏等以此並得选舉，武乃會宗亲，泣曰：“吾爲兄不肖，盗聲窃位，二弟長年，未豫荣禄，所以求得分財，自取大讥。

translations.literal: Villagers all praised the younger brothers' yielding and despised Wu's greed—Yan and the others thereby gained recommendation—Wu then assembled lineage kin—weeping: "I as elder brother was unworthy—stole reputation and position—two younger brothers grown yet never tasted glory—therefore I sought divided property—drawing great ridicule on myself.
translations.idiomatic: When his brothers won praise he revealed it was a ruse to spotlight them.

sentences.zh: 今理產所增，三倍于前，悉以推二弟，一無所留。

translations.literal: Now the estate's increase triples previous—all I push to the two brothers—I retain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He tripled their shares and kept nothing.

sentences.zh: ”于是郡中翕然，远近稱之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the commandery concurred—near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery applauded the stunt empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 位至長乐少府。

translations.literal: He rose to superintendent of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He became superintendent of Changle palace.

sentences.zh: 荆少爲郡吏，兄子世嘗报仇殺人，怨者操兵攻之。

translations.literal: Jing in youth was a commandery clerk—his elder brother's son Shi once avenged murder—the aggrieved seized weapons to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Xu Shi killed in blood feud; enemies came for revenge.

sentences.zh: 荆聞，乃出門逆怨者，跪而言曰：“世前無狀相犯，咎皆在荆不能训導。

translations.literal: Jing heard—went out gate to meet the aggrieved—knelt saying: "Shi formerly offended without cause—the fault lies entirely with Jing's failure to instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing knelt and blamed himself for the nephew's crime.

sentences.zh: 兄既早没，一子爲嗣，如令死者傷其灭絕，愿殺身代之。

translations.literal: The elder brother died early—one son continues the line—if the dead harm its extinction—I wish to substitute my body.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his life for his nephew's.

sentences.zh: ”怨家扶荆起，曰：“許掾郡中稱賢，吾何敢相侵？

translations.literal: " The enemy raised Jing—said: "Clerk Xu—the commandery calls worthy—how dare we attack?
translations.idiomatic: The feuding clan lifted him up—honoring his office.

sentences.zh: ”因遂委去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They walked away from the feud.

sentences.zh: 荆名誉益著。

translations.literal: Jing's reputation grew more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread.

sentences.zh: 太守黄兢舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Governor Huang Jing recommended him filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Huang Jing nominated him.

sentences.zh: 和帝時，稍遷桂陽太守。

translations.literal: Under Emperor He he was gradually promoted governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor He he rose to Guiyang governor.

sentences.zh: 郡濱南州，風俗脆薄，不識學義。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered the southern provinces—custom flimsy and thin—not knowing study and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Guiyang was shallow in learning.

sentences.zh: 荆爲設丧纪婚姻制度，使知禮禁。

translations.literal: Jing established mourning and marriage regulations—letting them know ritual prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: He codified funerals and weddings.

sentences.zh: 嘗行春到耒陽縣，人有蒋均者，兄弟爭財，互相言訟。

translations.literal: Once on spring circuit he reached Leiyang county—a man Jiang Jun—brothers quarreling over property—mutually sued.
translations.idiomatic: At Leiyang the Jiang brothers sued over inheritance.

sentences.zh: 荆對之嘆曰：“吾荷國重任，而教化不行，咎在太守。

translations.literal: Jing sighed at them: "I bear the state's heavy charge—yet transformation does not proceed—the fault lies with the governor.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed his own teaching for their quarrel.

sentences.zh: ”乃顾使吏上書陳狀，乞詣廷尉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon turned ordering clerks memorialize status—begging to go to the minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a report draft requesting his own impeachment.

sentences.zh: 均兄弟感悔，各求受罪。

translations.literal: Jun brothers felt shame—each sought punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers begged punishment instead.

sentences.zh: 在事十二年，父老稱歌。

translations.literal: Twelve years in office—elders sang praise.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years brought folk songs.

sentences.zh: 以病自上，征拜諫議大夫，卒于官。

translations.literal: Illness submitted upward—summoned remonstrance counselor—died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired reporting illness, became remonstrance counselor, died there.

sentences.zh: 桂陽人爲立廟树碑。

translations.literal: Guiyang people raised temple and stele.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang built him temple and stone.

sentences.zh: 荆孫𢒰，靈帝時爲太尉。

translations.literal: Jing's grandson Kan—under Emperor Ling became grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xu Kan served as grand commandant under Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗字伯周，會稽上虞上也。

translations.literal: Meng Chang, courtesy name Bozhou, was a man of Shangyu in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang, styled Bozhou, came from Shangyu in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其先三世爲郡吏，並伏節死難。

translations.literal: His ancestors for three generations were commandery clerks—all died holding integrity in disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of Mengs died serving the commandery honorably.

sentences.zh: 嘗少修操行，仕郡爲户曹史。

translations.literal: Chang in youth cultivated conduct—served the commandery as clerk of households.
translations.idiomatic: Young Meng Chang served as household clerk.

sentences.zh: 上虞有寡婦至孝養姑。

translations.literal: Shangyu had a widow utmost filial—nursing her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: A famously filial widow cared for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑年老寿終，夫女弟先懷嫌忌，乃诬婦厌苦供養，加鸩其母，列訟縣庭。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law aged and died of natural years—the husband's younger sister bore prior suspicion—thereupon slandered the widow—that she loathed the service—poisoned her mother—petitioned at county court.
translations.idiomatic: The sister-in-law framed her for poisoning the old woman.

sentences.zh: 郡不加寻察，遂结竟其罪。

translations.literal: The commandery did not pursue investigation—thereupon closed her guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The county rushed conviction without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 嘗先知枉狀，备言之于太守，太守不爲理。

translations.literal: Chang knew beforehand the injustice—fully spoke to the governor—the governor would not hear.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang pleaded her innocence in vain.

sentences.zh: 嘗哀泣外門，因謝病去，婦竟冤死。

translations.literal: Chang wept outside the gate—thereupon resigned illness—she ended dying wronged.
translations.idiomatic: He wept at the gate, quit, and she was executed innocent.

sentences.zh: 自是郡中連旱二年，祷請無所獲。

translations.literal: From this the commandery suffered drought two years—prayers gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Two years of drought followed.

sentences.zh: 后太守殷丹到官，訪問其故，嘗詣府具陳寡婦冤诬之事。

translations.literal: Later Governor Yin Dan arrived—asked the reason—Chang went to headquarters detailing the widow's false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yin Dan investigated; Meng Chang retold the frame.

sentences.zh: 因曰：“昔東海孝婦，感天致旱，于公一言，甘澤時降。

translations.literal: Then said: "Formerly the filial widow of Donghai moved heaven to drought—Magistrate Yu Gong's one word—sweet rain fell on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Donghai widow drought parable.

sentences.zh: 宜戮訟者，以謝冤魂，庶幽枉獲申，時雨可期。

translations.literal: We ought execute the accuser—to apologize to the wronged ghost—perhaps hidden wrong obtains redress—timely rain may be hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Execute the slanderer to appease her ghost and unlock rain.

sentences.zh: ”丹從之，即刑訟女而祭婦墓，天應澍雨，谷稼以登。

translations.literal: " Dan followed—immediately executed the accusing daughter—sacrificed at the widow's tomb—heaven answered with soaking rain—grain crops ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Dan executed the accuser; rain followed.

sentences.zh: 嘗后策孝廉，舉茂才，拜徐令。

translations.literal: Chang later passed filial and incorrupt—recommended flourishing talent—appointed magistrate of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He became Xu county magistrate after recommendations.

sentences.zh: 州郡表其能，遷合浦太守。

translations.literal: Province and commandery memorialized his ability—promoted governor of Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Hepu governor on merit.

sentences.zh: 郡不產谷實，而海出珠寶，与交阯比境，常通商贩，留籴粮食。

translations.literal: The commandery produced no grain yet the sea yielded pearls—bordering Jiaozhi—constantly traded merchant ships—stockpiling grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hepu lived on pearls and imported grain.

sentences.zh: 先時宰守並多貪秽，诡人采求，不知纪极，珠遂渐徙于交阯郡界。

translations.literal: Earlier governors mostly greedy and corrupt—deceive men to gather pearls—without limit—pearls gradually migrated to Jiaozhi's border.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy governors stripped the pearl beds until oysters fled to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 于是行旅不至，人物無资，貧者饿死于道。

translations.literal: Thereupon travelers did not arrive—people lacked resources—the poor starved dead on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Trade stopped and peasants starved.

sentences.zh: 嘗到官，革易前敝，求民病利。

translations.literal: Chang arrived at office—reformed prior abuses—sought the people's harms and profits.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang ended corruption and asked after livelihood.

sentences.zh: 曾未逾歲，去珠复還，百姓皆反其業，商貨流通，稱爲神明。

translations.literal: Within one year pearls returned—all commoners reversed to their occupations—merchant goods circulated—called divine.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls returned within the year—commerce revived—people called him divine.

sentences.zh: 以病自上，被征當還，吏民攀車請之。

translations.literal: Illness submitted upward—summoned should return—clerks and people clung to his carriage begging.
translations.idiomatic: Recall orders sent crowds clinging to his wheels.

sentences.zh: 嘗既不得進，乃載乡民船夜遁去。

translations.literal: Chang could not advance—thereupon boarded a villager's boat fleeing by night.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away by riverboat at night.

sentences.zh: 隱處穷澤，身自耕佣。

translations.literal: Hidden in poor marshes—personally plowing and hiring out.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed and hired out in hiding.

sentences.zh: 邻縣士民慕其德，就居止者百余家。

translations.literal: Neighboring county scholars and commoners admired his virtue—those settling near exceeded a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred households joined his colony.

sentences.zh: 榧龀桓帝時、尚書同郡杨乔上書薦嘗曰：

translations.literal: During Emperor Huan's reign Minister Yang Qiao of the same commandery memorialized recommending Chang:
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan Minister Yang Qiao from Kuaiji memorialized for Meng Chang:

sentences.zh: 臣前后七表言故合浦太守孟嘗，而身輕言微，終不蒙察。

translations.literal: Your servant seven times memorialized former Hepu Governor Meng Chang—yet body light speech slight—never received attention.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiao said seven petitions for Meng Chang went ignored.

sentences.zh: 区区破心，徒然而已。

translations.literal: My petty broken heart—was vain alone.
translations.idiomatic: His pleas seemed futile.

sentences.zh: 嘗安仁弘義，耽乐道德，清行出俗，能干絕群。

translations.literal: Chang embraces benevolence and enlarges righteousness—delights in virtue—pure conduct beyond custom—ability surpasses crowds.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Meng Chang's virtue and talent.

sentences.zh: 前更守宰，移風改政，去珠复還，飢民蒙活。

translations.literal: Earlier replacing governors—shifted winds reformed policy—pearls returned—starving people lived.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled how Meng Chang restored Hepu's pearls and saved lives.

sentences.zh: 且南海多珍，財產易積，掌握之内，價盈兼金，而嘗單身謝病，躬耕垄次，匿景藏采，不扬华藻。

translations.literal: Moreover South Sea abounds in treasures—wealth easily hoarded—within grasp—value doubles gold—yet Chang alone resigned illness—personally plowing ridge furrows—hiding brilliance—displaying no flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Meng Chang walked away from pearls worth gold to farm in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 實羽翮之美用，非徒腹背之毛也。

translations.literal: Truly wing-feathers' fine use—not merely belly-back down.
translations.idiomatic: He is wing-feather talent—not mere fluff.

sentences.zh: 而沉淪草莽，好爵莫及，廊廟之寶，棄于沟渠。

translations.literal: Yet sunk in weeds—good rank cannot reach—court treasures cast in ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Yet genius rots in ditches while court lacks ministers.

sentences.zh: 且年歲有讫，桑榆行盡，而忠贞之節，永謝圣時。

translations.literal: Moreover years have ends—mulberry and elm roads exhaust—yet loyalty's integrity forever leaves the sage hour.
translations.idiomatic: Years run out—loyal hearts waste unrealized.

sentences.zh: 臣誠傷心，私用流涕。

translations.literal: Your servant truly grieves—privately shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiao wept at the waste.

sentences.zh: 夫物以远至爲珍，士以稀見爲貴。

translations.literal: Things prized by distance arriving—scholars prized by rare sight.
translations.idiomatic: Rare goods and rare men deserve fetching.

sentences.zh: 槃木朽珠，爲萬乘用者，左右爲之容耳。

translations.literal: Warped wood or rotten pearl—what ten thousand carriages use—only because attendants polish them.
translations.idiomatic: Even flawed timber shines when courtiers buff it.

sentences.zh: 王者取士，宜拔衆之所貴。

translations.literal: Kings obtaining scholars—should elevate what crowds esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Thrones should elevate what the people prize.

sentences.zh: 臣以斗筲之姿，趨走日月之侧。

translations.literal: Your servant with dipper-measure stature—hurrying beside sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I am a minor clerk beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 思立微節，不敢苟私乡曲。

translations.literal: Thinking to establish slight integrity—dare not selfishly favor native lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I seek honest counsel beyond hometown bias.

sentences.zh: 窃感禽息，亡身進賢。

translations.literal: Privately moved by Qin Xi—dying body advancing worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Like Qin Xi dying to recommend talent.

sentences.zh: 嘗竟不見用。

translations.literal: Chang ended unused.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang never won office again.

sentences.zh: 年七十，卒于家。

translations.literal: At seventy sui he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at seventy.

sentences.zh: 第五訪

translations.literal: Fifth Fang
translations.idiomatic: Section heading for Fifth Fang (the Fifth lineage).

sentences.zh: 第五訪字仲谋，京兆長陵人，司空倫之族孫也。

translations.literal: Fifth Fang, courtesy name Zhongmou, was a man of Changling in the capital district—great-grandson of Minister of Works Di Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth Fang, styled Zhongmou, came from Changling and descended from Minister of Works Di Lun.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，常佣耕以養兄嫂。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor—he regularly hired out plowing to support elder brother and sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and orphaned, he farmed for hire to feed his brother's household.

sentences.zh: 有闲暇，則以學文。

translations.literal: When he had leisure—then he studied letters.
translations.idiomatic: He studied whenever field work allowed.

sentences.zh: 仕郡爲功曹，察孝廉，补新都令。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as merit assessor—investigated filial and incorrupt—appointed magistrate of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from merit assessor to magistrate of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 政平化行，三年之間，邻縣歸之，户口十倍。

translations.literal: Government level—transformation proceeding—within three years neighboring counties submitted—registered households multiplied tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: In three years fair rule drew neighbors and tenfold population.

sentences.zh: 遷張掖太守。

translations.literal: Promoted governor of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: He became Zhangye governor.

sentences.zh: 歲飢，粟石數千，訪乃开仓赈給以救其敝。

translations.literal: Year famine—grain cost thousands per shi—Fang then opened granaries and relieved to save their distress.
translations.idiomatic: When grain hit thousands per shi he opened the granaries.

sentences.zh: 更惧譴，爭欲上言。

translations.literal: Further fearing reprimand—they vied wishing to memorialize upward.
translations.idiomatic: Staff begged to clear the aid with the court first.

sentences.zh: 訪曰：“若上須报，是棄民也。

translations.literal: Fang said: "If upward must await reply—that is abandoning the people.
translations.idiomatic: He said waiting for approval meant abandoning the starving.

sentences.zh: 太守乐以一身救百姓！

translations.literal: A governor gladly uses one body to save the hundred surnames!
translations.idiomatic: "I will risk one life for the people."

sentences.zh: ”遂出谷賦人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon issued grain distributing to people.
translations.idiomatic: He released the grain.

sentences.zh: 順帝玺書嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun's imperial-seal letter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun sent sealed praise.

sentences.zh: 由是一郡得全。

translations.literal: From this one commandery wholly survived.
translations.idiomatic: The whole commandery survived.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，官民並豐，界無姦盗。

translations.literal: After more than a year—officials and commoners both abundant—the border without villain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year stores refilled and bandits vanished.

sentences.zh: 遷南陽太守，去官。

translations.literal: Promoted governor of Nanyang—left office.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly governed Nanyang then resigned.

sentences.zh: 拜護羌校尉，邊境服其威信。

translations.literal: Appointed colonel protecting the Qiang—the frontier submitted to his awesome trust.
translations.idiomatic: As colonel of the Qiang he commanded the border.

sentences.zh: 卒于官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in that post.

sentences.zh: 劉矩字叔方，沛國蕭人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ju, courtesy name Shufang, was a man of Xiao in the Principality of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ju, styled Shufang, came from Xiao in Pei.

sentences.zh: 叔父光，順帝時爲司徒。

translations.literal: Uncle Guang—under Emperor Shun was minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Liu Guang served Emperor Shun as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 矩少有高節，以父叔遼未得仕進，遂絕州郡之命。

translations.literal: Ju in youth had high integrity—because father Shu Liao had not obtained advancement—thereupon cut off province and commandery summons.
translations.idiomatic: He refused office until his father could advance.

sentences.zh: 太尉朱寵、太傅桓焉嘉其志義，故叔遼以此爲諸公所辟，拜議郎，矩乃舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhu Chong and Grand Tutor Huan Yan admired his resolve—therefore Shu Liao was summoned by the excellencies—appointed deliberation gentleman—Ju then was recommended filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Notables forced his father into office first; then Liu Ju accepted nomination.

sentences.zh: 稍遷雍丘令，以禮讓化之，其無孝義者，皆感悟自革。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted magistrate of Yongqiu—using ritual yielding to transform them—those without filial righteousness—all moved and reformed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiu he taught deference until the unruly reformed.

sentences.zh: 民有爭訟，矩常引之于前，提耳训告，以爲忿恚可忍，縣官不可入，使歸更寻思。

translations.literal: When commoners had lawsuits—Ju often led them before him—pulling ears instructing—thinking resentment can be endured—magistrate court must not be entered—sent them home to rethink.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled disputants aside and sent them home to cool off.

sentences.zh: 訟者感之，輒各罷去。
