translations.literal: The litigants were moved—each then stopped and left.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped suits without trial.

sentences.zh: 其有路得遺者，皆推寻其主。

translations.literal: Those who found things on the road—all traced and returned to owners.
translations.idiomatic: Lost property went back to owners.

sentences.zh: 在縣四年，以母忧去官。

translations.literal: Four years in county—because mother mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He quit for mourning after four years.

sentences.zh: 后太尉胡廣舉矩賢良方正，四遷爲尚書令。

translations.literal: Later Grand Commandant Hu Guang recommended Ju worthy and good honest and upright—four promotions to director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's recommendation lifted him to director of masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 矩性亮直，不能諧附貴勢，以是失大將軍梁冀意，出爲常山相，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Ju's nature bright and straight—could not harmonize with noble power—thereby losing Grand General Liang Ji's favor—sent out as chancellor of Changshan—illness left office.
translations.idiomatic: His honesty crossed Liang Ji; demoted to Changshan, he quit ill.

sentences.zh: 時冀妻兄孫祉爲沛相，矩惧爲所害，不敢還乡里，乃投彭城友人家。

translations.literal: At that time Ji's wife's elder brother Sun Zhi was chancellor of Pei—Ju feared harm—dared not return to village—thereupon fled to a friend's house in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Liang Ji's brother-in-law Sun Zhi, he hid in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，冀意少悟，乃止。

translations.literal: After more than a year Ji's intent slightly relented—thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Liang Ji cooled and left him alone.

sentences.zh: 补從事中郎，复爲尚書令，遷宗正、太常。

translations.literal: Appointed attendant gentleman—again director of masters of writing—promoted minister of the imperial clan and minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as minister of the imperial clan and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 延熹四年，代黄琼爲太尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth Yanxi year he replaced Huang Qiong as grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 161 he succeeded Huang Qiong as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 琼复爲司空，矩与琼及司徒种暠同心輔政，號爲賢相。

translations.literal: Qiong again became minister of works—Ju with Qiong and Minister of Education Chong Hao together assisted policy—called worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a praised trio with Huang Qiong and Chong Hao.

sentences.zh: 時，連有灾異，司隶校尉以劾三公。

translations.literal: At that time disasters linked in succession—colonel director of retainers impeached the Three Ducal Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Serial omens brought impeachment of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 尚書朱穆上疏，稱矩等良輔，以言殷汤、高宗不罪臣下之義。

translations.literal: Director of Masters of Writing Zhu Mu presented memorial—praising Ju and others as fine assistants—citing Shang Tang and Gaozong not blaming ministers' meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mu cited sage kings who spared ministers during calamity.

sentences.zh: 帝不省，竟以蛮夷反叛免。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed—finally because barbarians rebelled dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored Zhu Mu and fired the dukes over frontier revolt.

sentences.zh: 后复拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later again appointed grand palace counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as grand palace counselor.

sentences.zh: 靈帝初，代周景爲太尉。

translations.literal: Early Emperor Ling—replaced Zhou Jing as grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling he again replaced Zhou Jing as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 矩再爲上公，所辟召皆名儒宿德。

translations.literal: Ju twice being highest duke—those he summoned were all famed Confucians of established virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He packed his bureau with renowned scholars.

sentences.zh: 不与州郡交通。

translations.literal: Did not traffic with provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He took no gifts from local officials.

sentences.zh: 順辭默諫，多見省用。

translations.literal: Submissive words silent remonstrance—often adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His quiet counsel often shaped policy.

sentences.zh: 复以日食免。

translations.literal: Again because solar eclipse dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Another eclipse cost him his seal.

sentences.zh: 因乞骸骨，卒于家。

translations.literal: Thereupon begging bones—died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉寵字祖荣，東莱牟平人，劉悼惠王之后也。

translations.literal: Liu Chong, courtesy name Zurong, was a man of Muping in Donglai—descendant of Prince Dao Hui of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong of Muping descended from Prince Dao Hui.

sentences.zh: 悼惠王子孝王將闾，將闾少子封牟平侯，子孫家焉。

translations.literal: Prince Dao Hui's son Filial Prince Jianglü Jin—Jianglü's youngest son enfeoffed marquis of Muping—descendants settled there.
translations.idiomatic: The line settled Muping from a cadet marquisate.

sentences.zh: 父丕，博學，號爲通儒。

translations.literal: Father Pi—broadly learned—called thorough Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Pi was famed as a polymath.

sentences.zh: 寵少受父業，以明經舉孝廉，陳東平陵令，以仁惠爲吏民所爱。

translations.literal: Chong in youth received father's teaching—recommended filial and incorrupt on classics—appointed magistrate of Dongpingling in Chen—by benevolence and kindness loved by clerks and people.
translations.idiomatic: Classics degree won him Dongpingling magistrate—beloved for kindness.

sentences.zh: 母疾，棄官去。

translations.literal: Mother ill—abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 百姓將送塞道，車不得進，乃輕服遁歸。

translations.literal: Common people escorting filled the road—carriages could not advance—thereupon light dress slipped away returning.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds blocked his cart so he fled incognito.

sentences.zh: 后四遷爲豫章太守，又三遷拜會稽太守。

translations.literal: Later four promotions governor of Yuzhang—again three promotions appointed governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Yuzhang then Kuaiji governor.

sentences.zh: 山民愿朴，乃有白首不入市井者，頗爲官吏所扰。

translations.literal: Mountain people simple and honest—some white-haired never entering market—rather disturbed by clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Hill folk had never seen a market until corrupt runners harassed them.

sentences.zh: 寵简除烦苛，禁察非法，郡中大化。

translations.literal: Chong simplified and removed vexing severity—forbade and inspected illegal acts—the commandery greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped petty regulations and cleaned up extortion.

sentences.zh: 征爲將作大匠。

translations.literal: Summoned superintendent of public works.
translations.idiomatic: Recall made him superintendent of public works.

sentences.zh: 山陰縣有五六老叟，尨眉皓發，自若邪山谷間出，人赍百錢以送寵。

translations.literal: Shanyin county had five or six old men—shaggy brows white hair—emerging from between Mount Ye valleys—each carrying a hundred cash to send Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Five graybeards from Ye Valley brought a hundred cash each.

sentences.zh: 寵劳之曰：“父老何自苦？

translations.literal: Chong urged them: "Elders why trouble yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: He asked why they came.

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“山谷鄙生，未嘗識郡朝。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Valley bumpkins—never knew commandery court.
translations.idiomatic: They said they never visited the yamen before.

sentences.zh: 它守時吏發求民間，至夜不絕，或狗吠竟夕，民不得安。

translations.literal: Other governors' clerks issued searches among people—reaching night without cease—or dogs barked all night—people could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Past magistrates sent night searches and barking dogs.

sentences.zh: 自明府下車以来，狗不夜吠，民不見吏。

translations.literal: Since enlightened prefect stepped down from carriage—dogs do not bark at night—people do not see clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Chong dogs slept and clerks vanished from villages.

sentences.zh: 年老遭值圣明，今聞當見棄去，故自扶奉送。

translations.literal: Old age meets sage clarity—now hearing should be cast aside leaving—therefore supporting ourselves to escort.
translations.idiomatic: They feared losing him to promotion.

sentences.zh: ”寵曰：“吾政何能及公言邪？

translations.literal: " Chong said: "How can my governance reach your words?
translations.idiomatic: He protested unworthiness.

sentences.zh: 勤苦父老！

translations.literal: Toiling elders!
translations.idiomatic: "You honor me too much."

sentences.zh: ”爲人选一大錢受之。

translations.literal: " For each man chose one large cash and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted one large coin from each elder.

sentences.zh: 轉爲宗正、大鸿胪。

translations.literal: Transferred minister of the imperial clan—grand herald.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to minister of the imperial clan and grand herald.

sentences.zh: 延熹四年，代黄琼爲司空、以陰雾愆陽免。

translations.literal: Fourth Yanxi year—replaced Huang Qiong as minister of works—dismissed because yin miasma offended yang.
translations.idiomatic: In 161 he became minister of works but fell to weather omens.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜將作大匠，得爲宗正。

translations.literal: Shortly—appointed superintendent of public works—obtained minister of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to public works and the imperial clan ministry.

sentences.zh: 建宁元年，代王暢爲司空，频遷司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: First Jianning year—replaced Wang Chang as minister of works—repeatedly promoted minister of education—grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 168 he climbed to minister of education and grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 二年，以日食策免，歸乡里。

translations.literal: Second year—because solar eclipse edict dismissed—returned village.
translations.idiomatic: A 169 eclipse ended his career.

sentences.zh: 寵前后历宰二郡，累登卿相，而清約省素，家無貨積。

translations.literal: Chong front and back governed two commanderies—ascended repeatedly to ministers—yet pure frugal plain—household without hoarded goods.
translations.idiomatic: Despite top posts he died poor.

sentences.zh: 嘗出京師，欲息亭舍，亭吏止之，曰：“整頓洒埽，以待劉公，不可得止。

translations.literal: Once leaving capital—wished to rest post station—post clerk stopped him—said: "We tidy and sweep—awaiting Lord Liu—cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: An inn kept a room reserved for him alone.

sentences.zh: ”寵無言而去，時人稱其長者。

translations.literal: " Chong spoke nothing and left—men of the time called him elder.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away without argument—praised as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以老病卒于家。

translations.literal: Because old illness died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Old age took him at home.

sentences.zh: 弟方，官至山陽太守。

translations.literal: Younger brother Fang—rose to governor of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Liu Fang governed Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 方有二子：貸字公山，繇字正禮。

translations.literal: Fang had two sons—Dai courtesy Gongshan—Yao courtesy Zhengli.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang's sons were Liu Dai and Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 兄弟劉名稱。

translations.literal: The brothers won fame under the Liu name.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers became famous as Lius.

sentences.zh: 董卓入洛陽，岱從侍中出爲兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo entered Luoyang—Dai from attendant inside went out inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's coup sent Liu Dai to Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 虚己爱物，爲士人所附。

translations.literal: Emptying self cherishing things—scholar-officials attached.
translations.idiomatic: Humility won the gentry.

sentences.zh: 初平三年，青州黄巾贼入兗州，殺任城相鄭遂，轉入東平。

translations.literal: Third Chuping year—Qingzhou Yellow Turbans entered Yan Province—killed minister of state Zheng Sui—turned into Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In 192 Yellow Turbans killed Zheng Sui and swept Dongping.

sentences.zh: 岱擊之，戰死。

translations.literal: Dai struck them—died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai fell fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 興平中，繇爲杨州牧、振威將軍。

translations.literal: In Xingping years—Yao was Yang Province shepherd—general who displays might.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingping Liu Yao became Yang inspector.

sentences.zh: 時袁术據淮南，繇乃移居曲阿。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shu held Huainan—Yao thereupon moved residence to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu drove him to Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 值中國丧亂，士友多南奔，繇携接收養，与同优剧，甚得名稱。

translations.literal: Meeting central plain chaos—scholar friends mostly fled south—Yao led receiving and nurturing—sharing hardship—greatly won famed praise.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered refugee scholars and earned renown.

sentences.zh: 袁术遣孫策攻破繇，因奔豫章，病卒。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu dispatched Sun Ce to break Yao—thereupon fled to Yuzhang—died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce broke him; he died fleeing to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 仇覽字季智，一名香，除留考城人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Lan, courtesy name Jizhi—also named Xiang—was a man of Kaocheng in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lan, also Xiang, came from Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 少爲書生淳默，乡里無知者。

translations.literal: In youth was student pure silent—village knew him not.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful bookworm—locally obscure.

sentences.zh: 年四十，縣召补史，选爲蒲亭長。

translations.literal: At forty sui county summoned supplement clerk—selected chief of Pu pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he became Pu pavilion chief.

sentences.zh: 勸人生業，爲制科令，至于果菜爲限，鸡豕有數，农事既毕，乃令子弟群居，還就黉學。

translations.literal: Urged people to pursue livelihood—made regulations—even fruit and vegetables had limits—chickens and pigs had numbers—when farming finished—ordered youths group dwell—return to school.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated farm quotas and idle youths' schooling.

sentences.zh: 其剽輕游恣者，皆役以田桑，严設科罰。

translations.literal: Those reckless roaming—all worked fields and mulberry—strictly set regulations and fines.
translations.idiomatic: He fined loafers into farm labor.

sentences.zh: 躬助丧事，赈恤穷寡。

translations.literal: Personally aided funerals—relieved poor widows.
translations.idiomatic: He buried the poor and fed widows.

sentences.zh: 期年稱大化。

translations.literal: Within a full year called great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the district turned around.

sentences.zh: 覽初到亭，人有陳元者，独与母居，而母詣覽告元不孝。

translations.literal: When Lan first reached pavilion—there was a man Chen Yuan—alone dwelling with mother—yet mother went to Lan accusing Yuan unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: A mother accused son Chen Yuan of filial failure.

sentences.zh: 覽驚曰：“吾近日過舍，庐落整頓，耕耘以時。

translations.literal: Lan startled said: "I recently passed house—homestead tidy—plowing and weeding on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Lan saw tidy fields and doubted the charge.

sentences.zh: 此非恶人，當是教化未及至耻。

translations.literal: This is not evil man—should be transformation not yet arrived to shame.
translations.idiomatic: He called it failed instruction, not evil.

sentences.zh: 母守寡養孤，苦身投老，奈何肆忿于一朝，欲致子以不義乎？

translations.literal: Mother guarding widow raising orphan—bittering body reaching old age—how vent wrath in one morning—wish to bring son to unfilial?
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether rage would brand her son unfilial.

sentences.zh: ”母聞感悔，涕泣而去。

translations.literal: " Mother hearing felt shame—weeping departed.
translations.idiomatic: The mother withdrew weeping.

sentences.zh: 覽乃亲到元家，与其母子飲，因爲節人倫孝行，譬以祸福之言。

translations.literal: Lan then personally reached Yuan's house—drank with mother and son—thereupon regulated human relations filial conduct—likening fortune and disaster words.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the family and lectured on filial duty.

sentences.zh: 元卒成孝子。

translations.literal: Yuan finally became filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan became a model son.

sentences.zh: 乡邑爲之諺曰：“父母何在在我庭，化我鳲枭哺所生。

translations.literal: District made proverb saying: "Where are parents—in my courtyard—transforming me owl feeding what bore it.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers sang a proverb about owls turned nurturing.
Here the proverb ends.

sentences.zh: 時考城令河内王渙，政尚严猛，聞覽以德化人，署爲主簿。

translations.literal: At that time Kaocheng Magistrate Wang Huan of Henei—administration valued stern severity—heard Lan transformed people with virtue—appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh magistrate Wang Huan of Kaocheng made Qiu Lan his chief clerk after hearing how he reformed Chen Yuan.

sentences.zh: 謂覽曰：“主簿聞陳元之過，不罪而化之，得無少鹰鹯之志邪？

translations.literal: He said to Lan: "Chief clerk heard Chen Yuan's fault—did not punish but transformed him—does it not lack a bit of hawk and shrike spirit?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan asked if mercy meant weak resolve.

sentences.zh: ”覽曰：“以爲鹰鹯，不若鸾鳳。

translations.literal: " Lan said: "To be hawk and shrike—not equal to luan and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lan preferred phoenix virtue to raptor law.

sentences.zh: ”渙謝遣曰：“枳棘非鸾鳳所栖，百里岂大賢之路？

translations.literal: " Huan apologized and sent off saying: "Thorn brambles are not where luan and phoenix roost—can a hundred li be the great worthy's path?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan admitted a petty magistracy unworthy of him.

sentences.zh: 今日太學曳長裾，飞名誉，皆主簿后耳。

translations.literal: Today Imperial Academy trailing long robes—flying fame and reputation—all trail chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He said the capital's celebrities walked in Qiu Lan's shadow.

sentences.zh: 以一月奉爲资，勉卒景行。

translations.literal: Take one month salary as capital—strive to finish lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He funded Lan's academy year with one month's pay.
Here Wang Huan's speech ends.

sentences.zh: 覽入太學。

translations.literal: Lan entered Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lan enrolled at the academy.

sentences.zh: 時，諸生同郡符融有高名，与覽比宇，賓客盈室。

translations.literal: At that time student Fu Rong of the same commandery had high fame—with Lan neighboring chambers—guests filled his room.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong next door drew crowds while Qiu Lan stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 覽常自守，不与融言。

translations.literal: Lan constantly guarded himself alone—not speaking with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Fu Rong's chat.

sentences.zh: 融觀其容止，心独奇之，乃謂曰：“与先生同郡壤，邻房牖。

translations.literal: Rong observing his bearing—alone thought him strange—thereupon said: "With sir same commandery soil—neighboring window chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong wondered why he stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 今京師英雄四集，志士交结之秋，雖務經常，守之何因？

translations.literal: Now capital heroes gather from four directions—season for stalwarts to ally—though you pursue classics—what cause to guard silence?
translations.idiomatic: Fu urged networking in the capital.

sentences.zh: ”覽乃正色曰：“天子修設太學，岂但使人游談其中！

translations.literal: " Lan then sternly colored said: "The Son of Heaven established Imperial Academy—did it only intend men to gossip therein!
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lan snapped that the academy was not a salon.

sentences.zh: ”高揖而去，不复与言。

translations.literal: " Bowed high and left—no longer spoke with him.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed off and cut Fu Rong cold.

sentences.zh: 后融以告郭林宗，林宗因与融赍刺就房谒之，遂請留宿。

translations.literal: Later Rong told Guo Tai—Tai therefore with Rong carrying visiting cards went to chamber paying respects—thereupon asked him stay overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai heard from Fu Rong and visited with cards.

sentences.zh: 林宗嗟嘆，下床爲拜。

translations.literal: Tai sighed—stepped down from couch and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai bowed from his seat in respect.

sentences.zh: 覽學毕歸乡里，州郡並請，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: Lan finished study returning village—province and commandery together summoned—all declined illness.
translations.idiomatic: After graduation he refused every appointment.

sentences.zh: 雖在宴居，必以禮自整。

translations.literal: Although at leisure dwelling—must by ritual self-rectify.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he kept ritual discipline.

sentences.zh: 妻子有過，輒免冠自責。

translations.literal: When wife and children faulted—always doffed cap self-blaming.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed himself before correcting family.

sentences.zh: 妻子庭謝，候覽冠，乃敢升堂。

translations.literal: Wife and children courtyard apologized—waited Lan's cap—then dared ascend hall.
translations.idiomatic: Kin could not re-enter until he replaced his cap.

sentences.zh: 家人莫見喜怒聲色之異。

translations.literal: Household never saw difference in joy anger voice color.
translations.idiomatic: His household never saw his temper.

sentences.zh: 后征方正，遇疾而卒。

translations.literal: Later summoned worthy and good honest—met illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died when summoned as an outstanding candidate.

sentences.zh: 三子皆有文史才，少子玄，最知名。

translations.literal: Three sons all had literary and historical talent—youngest son Xuan—most famed.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons were scholars; youngest Qiu Xuan most noted.

sentences.zh: 童恢字漢宗，琅邪姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Tong Hui, courtesy name Hanzong, was a man of Gumu in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Hui, styled Hanzong, came from Gumu in Langya.

sentences.zh: 父仲玉，遭玉凶荒，倾家赈恤，九族乡里赖全者以百數。

translations.literal: Father Zhongyu—met jade-like famine year—emptied household relieving—nine clans and village relied on survival—numbered in hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong Zhongyu spent the family fortune in famine to save hundreds.

sentences.zh: 仲玉早卒。

translations.literal: Zhongyu died early.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Zhongyu died young.

sentences.zh: 恢少仕州郡爲吏，司徒杨賜聞其执法廉平，乃辟之。

translations.literal: Hui in youth served province and commandery as clerk—Minister of Education Yang Ci heard his law enforcement honest and level—thereupon summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ci recruited him for fair justice.

sentences.zh: 乃賜被劾當免，掾属悉投刺去，恢独詣阙爭之。

translations.literal: When Ci faced impeachment should be dismissed—clerks and aides all cast visiting cards and left—Hui alone went to palace gate disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ci faced impeachment only Tong Hui pleaded at court.

sentences.zh: 乃得理，掾属悉歸府，恢杖策而逝。

translations.literal: Thereupon obtained justice—clerks and aides all returned to bureau—Hui cane in hand departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ci was cleared; Tong Hui quit once staff returned.

sentences.zh: 由是論者歸美。

translations.literal: From this debaters returned praise.
translations.idiomatic: Critics praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 复辟公府，除不其令。

translations.literal: Again summoned to excellency bureau—appointed magistrate of Buqi.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Buqi county.

sentences.zh: 吏人有犯违禁法，輒隨方晓示。

translations.literal: When clerks and people violated prohibitions and laws—always according to situation dawn explained.
translations.idiomatic: He coached offenders instead of jailing them first.

sentences.zh: 若吏稱其職，人行善事者，皆賜以酒肴之禮，以勸勵之。

translations.literal: If clerks praised their office—people walked good deeds—all bestowed wine and meat ritual—to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted honest clerks and good villagers.

sentences.zh: 耕織种收，皆有条章。

translations.literal: Plowing weaving planting harvesting—all had regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Farm work ran by written rules.

sentences.zh: 一境清靜，牢狱連年無囚。

translations.literal: Whole territory quiet—prison years without prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: His jail stood empty for years.

sentences.zh: 比縣流人歸化，徙居二萬餘户。

translations.literal: Neighboring county wandering people submitted to transformation—moved dwelling exceeding twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand refugee households settled.

sentences.zh: 民嘗爲虎所害，乃設槛捕之，生獲二虎。

translations.literal: Commoners once harmed by tigers—thereupon set traps capturing—alive obtained two tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Traps caught two man-eating tigers alive.

sentences.zh: 恢聞而出，咒虎曰：“天生萬物，唯人爲貴。

translations.literal: Hui heard and came out—charged the tigers: "Heaven bore the myriad things—only man is noble.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Hui lectured the penned tigers.

sentences.zh: 虎狼當食六畜，而残暴于人。

translations.literal: Tigers and wolves ought eat six domestic animals—yet cruelly harm people.
translations.idiomatic: He said beasts should eat livestock, not men.

sentences.zh: 王法殺人者傷，傷人則論法。

translations.literal: Kingly law—killers die—wounders face statute.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Han homicide law.

sentences.zh: 汝若是殺人者，當垂頭服罪；

translations.literal: If you are killer—ought hang head confess guilt;
translations.idiomatic: If guilty, bow your head.

sentences.zh: 自知非者，當號呼稱冤。

translations.literal: If know yourself not—ought cry out claiming injustice.
translations.idiomatic: If innocent, cry out.

sentences.zh: ”一虎低頭閉目，狀如震惧，即時殺之。

translations.literal: " One tiger lowered head closed eyes—appearance like trembling fear—immediately killed it.
translations.idiomatic: One tiger slumped—he executed it.

sentences.zh: 其一視恢鳴吼，踊跃自奋，遂令放释。

translations.literal: The other viewing Hui roared—leaped self-exerting—thereupon ordered release.
translations.idiomatic: The other roared defiance—he freed it.

sentences.zh: 吏人爲之歌頌。

translations.literal: Clerks and people for him sang praise.
translations.idiomatic: Locals sang his tiger trial.

sentences.zh: 青州舉尤異，遷丹陽太守，暴疾而卒。

translations.literal: Qing Province recommended especially unusual—promoted governor of Danyang—sudden illness died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Danyang governor, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 弟翊字漢文，名高于恢，宰府先辟之。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yi courtesy Hanwen—name higher than Hui—excellency bureau first summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Tong Yi was more famous and summoned first.

sentences.zh: 翊陽喑不肯仕，及恢被命，乃就孝廉，除須昌長。

translations.literal: Yi feigned dumb refusing office—when Hui received appointment—then accepted filial and incorrupt—appointed chief of Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yi pretended muteness until his brother took office, then served.

sentences.zh: 化有異政，吏人生爲立碑。

translations.literal: Transformation had unusual administration—clerks and people raised stele while living.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang built him a living stele.

sentences.zh: 聞舉將丧，棄官歸。

translations.literal: Hearing recommending patron died—abandoned office returned.
translations.idiomatic: He quit on his patron's death.

sentences.zh: 后舉茂才，不就。

translations.literal: Later recommended flourishing talent—did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined a flourishing talent call.

sentences.zh: 卒于家。

translations.literal: Died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.
